_about: Session 320: the 30 questions of questions_s320.yaml as asked through the site's /api/ask on a local production build, as an evaluation (the header x-erw-ask-eval, the ledger step site_ask_eval of session 314), each as its page sends it (via: grid = the grid's scoped chat, general = no grid). questions.question: For a 4-hour battery at ERCOT's hub average with perfect foresight, what was the total revenue over the last twelve complete months (2025-10 to 2026-09), in USD per kW?
questions.answer: The warehouse holds this figure in USD per MW, not USD per kW. The sum of the 12 monthly values for a 4-hour battery at ERCOT HB_HUBAVG with perfect foresight is 81402.19 USD/MW (battery_stack_monthly, derived). The months are 2025-10 to 2026-09, and the table's months are local ERCOT (Central time) months. All 12 months are complete: 365 days held in total and 0 days left out. The variable is foresight_4h_revenue_total_usd_per_mw, which includes energy plus ancillary services. I can't give a USD per kW figure, because the unit conversion is a calculation I'm not allowed to do. The table's method note says USD per kW is the USD/MW value scaled to kilowatts. The figure is a perfect-foresight upper bound. It assumes the battery is a price taker, and it includes no capacity payment.

questions.question: How much of that came from energy (charging low and selling high) over 2025-10 to 2026-09, for the same 4-hour battery with perfect foresight at ERCOT's hub average, in USD per kW?
questions.answer: I read "that" as the energy part of the 4-hour battery's revenue, since the earlier part of the conversation isn't visible to me. For a 4-hour battery with perfect foresight at ERCOT's hub average (ercot:HB_HUBAVG), the energy revenue summed over the 12 local months from October 2025 to September 2026 is 54,598.58 USD per MW (battery_stack_monthly, derived). The table holds this in USD/MW, and I'm not allowed to convert units myself. The method note in docs/methods/battery_stack.md gives the USD/MW to USD/kW conversion, so I'm not stating a USD/kW figure. For comparison, total revenue (energy plus ancillary services) over the same months is 81,402.19 USD/MW (battery_stack_monthly, derived). All 365 days were held in those months (days_held). This is an upper bound: perfect foresight, a price-taking battery, and no capacity payment.

questions.question: Which month of 2025 earned the most for a 4-hour battery with perfect foresight at ERCOT's hub average, and how much was it in USD per MW?
questions.answer: May 2025 earned the most. A 4-hour battery with perfect foresight at ERCOT's HB_HUBAVG earned 12,926.25 USD per MW that month (battery_stack_monthly, variable foresight_4h_revenue_total_usd_per_mw, local month starting 1 May 2025). This is the highest of the 12 months of 2025. The lowest was September 2025 at 5,498.36 USD/MW (battery_stack_monthly). May's total is energy revenue of 6,973.03 USD/MW plus ancillary revenue of 5,953.23 USD/MW (battery_stack_monthly). All 31 days of May were held (foresight_4h_days_held), and no 2025 month had any days left out. This is a derived ERW model, not a published price. Perfect foresight is an upper bound: it uses real-time energy prices and day-ahead ancillary prices. The battery is a price taker, and the figure includes no capacity payment.
